clue.text: Religious type guards gold for speculator

indicators.note: to guard is to surround protectively, so one word's letters are placed around the other's

parts.note: a theist is a believer in God
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A churchgoer keeps a hoard of gold while dabbling in risky investments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious type' looks like the definition, but it supplies the outer word; OR is heraldry's word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist is someone who forms ideas and hypotheses, i.e. one who speculates.

clue.text: Pattern produced by an employee, occasionally delayed

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker hired now and then
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A design is produced by a worker who sometimes turns up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' looks like it picks alternate letters, but it describes the temporary worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a model or guide used for making copies.

clue.text: Lexicographers wanting diagram resorted to this strange device

indicators.note: re-sorted, sorted again, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
wanting means lacking, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a graph is a kind of diagram

explanation.surface: Dictionary makers without a chart turned to this odd gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing GRAPH from LEXICOGRAPHERS leaves LEXICOERS, which 'resorted' (re-sorted) rearranges. In Longfellow's poem a banner bore 'a strange device, Excelsior!'
explanation.definitionFit: Longfellow's poem describes a youth carrying a banner with this motto, called 'a strange device'.

clue.text: Frenchman and wife start again

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A French husband and his spouse make a fresh beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to resume or begin afresh.

clue.text: Removed from person's car if you criticise hurtfully

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the run of words, extracted rather than built

explanation.surface: Something has been taken out of someone's car if you slate them.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies across 'person's car if you'.
explanation.definitionFit: To scarify is to wound with harsh criticism, figuratively scratching.

clue.text: Person who's attacked two little boys

parts.note: Vic is a short form of the boy's name Victor
Tim is a short form of the boy's name Timothy

explanation.surface: Someone has been set upon by a couple of young lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' tells you the boys' names are shortened forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A victim is anyone who suffers an assault or harm.

clue.text: Start nine or ten trains moving without delay

indicators.note: the letters move around into a fresh order, like trains moving off

explanation.surface: Get nine or ten trains running immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges TEN TRAINS; 'Start nine or' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is a legal or formal word meaning immediately.

clue.text: Fine and grand affair

parts.note: fine thread is thin
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An elegant and splendid party.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing can mean an event or matter, as in 'a strange business'.

clue.text: Original expert

explanation.surface: An inventive specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A master copy is the source from which duplicates are made; a master is also a highly skilled practitioner.

clue.text: Projections available to public here show what directors have achieved

explanation.surface: Public screenings reveal what film-makers have accomplished.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture house is where films are projected for an audience; the word also means film-making as an art.

clue.text: Having this, able to keep dry wine

parts.note: a mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat that keeps the wearer dry
to have a garment on is to be wearing it

explanation.surface: A wine with a quality that will keep things dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically: with your raincoat on you stay dry, so MAC and ON join. Mac is the everyday British word for a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Macon is a Burgundy wine from the area around the French town of that name.

clue.text: Centrally placed on board, MP aids his constituents

indicators.note: the parts making up the phrase, its constituents, are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: An MP helps the voters in his constituency, playing a central role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' looks like an MP's voters but signals rearranging the letters of MP AIDS HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, midway between bow and stern is the middle position.

clue.text: Pure flower found by naturalist

parts.note: the lily is a flower
Gilbert White was an 18th-century English naturalist, author of The Natural History of Selborne

explanation.surface: A spotless bloom is discovered by a nature lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert White is the famous naturalist of Selborne, a Hampshire village.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as white as a lily is spotless, figuratively innocent or untainted.

clue.text: Old German's point of view

explanation.surface: An ancient Teuton's way of looking at things.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were a Germanic tribe who settled in England; a particular perspective on a matter is also called this.

clue.text: Wanting a drink? Try this rum!

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the words are rearranged into an odd order

explanation.surface: A drinks offer: parched? Have some of this rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink on offer but is the old adjective meaning 'odd', signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being parched means you want liquid to drink.

clue.text: What's the matter with driver's attitude after vehicle turned over?

indicators.note: after places the attitude word behind the overturned vehicle in the answer
turned over suggests the vehicle flipped, so its word is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a golfer about to use a driver takes up a stance

explanation.surface: Asking what is wrong with a motorist's behaviour after his car overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' and 'after' order the pieces. The 'driver' is a golf club, not a motorist: a golfer adopts a set posture before swinging it.
explanation.definitionFit: Substance is physical matter, the material something is made of.

clue.text: Constable or sergeant, say

parts.note: reads as police ranks, but John Constable and John Singer Sargent (sounding like sergeant) were painters

explanation.surface: Examples of police ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: The police ranks mislead: Constable was an English landscape painter, and Sargent, sounding like 'sergeant', a portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Both men were painters, i.e. creators of fine art.

clue.text: Something's wrong — no end of trouble for composer

indicators.note: the letters are set wrong, put into a muddled order
the end of the word trouble is its final letter

explanation.surface: Something has gone wrong and caused endless trouble for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMETHINGS less the E at the end of 'trouble' ('no') leaves letters that 'wrong' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A songsmith is a writer of songs.

clue.text: Perennial gardener's wife put in flower borders? Not a lot!

indicators.note: one piece is put inside another
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Eve was the wife of Adam, the first gardener in Eden
few means not many

explanation.surface: A gardener's wife plants a handful of perennials in the flower beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower borders' gives F and R, the first and last letters of 'flower'; 'put in' places EVE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverfew is a herbaceous plant that comes back every year.

clue.text: Did some careful digging for foundation

parts.note: pro is Latin-derived for 'in favour of'
a bed is a base layer, as in a bed of concrete

explanation.surface: An archaeologist excavated carefully to find a building's base.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate closely, physically or figuratively, is to explore with a tool or questions.

clue.text: Failing to join the opposition

explanation.surface: Failing to sign up with the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a flaw; to defect is to desert one's side for its rival.

clue.text: Dog losing tail in snare

indicators.note: the dog's name loses its tail, meaning its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a springer is a breed of spaniel

explanation.surface: A dog's tail gets caught in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing tail' drops the last R of SPRINGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A springe is a noose trap for small game or birds.

clue.text: Mineral (about a gram) needed for plant

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: spinel is a hard crystalline mineral
g is the abbreviation for a gram

explanation.surface: A gram or so of mineral is required for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SPINEL around G.
explanation.definitionFit: Spignel, also called baldmoney, is a fragrant umbelliferous herb.

clue.text: Dog enjoyed being included in broadcast

indicators.note: one word is placed within another

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it by scattering
to have had something can mean to have enjoyed it

explanation.surface: A dog loved being featured on a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' means scattering seed, not a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, to tail.

clue.text: Composer gets time to relax before end of concert

parts.note: hols is British slang for holidays

indicators.note: the end of the word concert is its final letter

explanation.surface: A musician takes a break before the concert finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLS is British informal for holidays; Gustav Holst wrote The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was an English writer of music, best known for The Planets suite.

clue.text: Liberal introducing novel proposition in argument

parts.note: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen

explanation.surface: A Liberal brings a new idea into a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new' but means Jane Austen's book; 'introducing' places L first.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic and mathematics a lemma is an auxiliary premise used in a proof.

clue.text: I caught fool tucking into spare stew

indicators.note: the three pieces tuck themselves inside the other word, like food tucked into

parts.note: spare and free both mean available, unoccupied
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to catching an idiot eating a leftover casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare' as an adjective means free, not extra; 'tucking into' looks like eating but places the pieces inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a dish of meat cut up and cooked in a thick sauce.

clue.text: In pursuit of king a short distance in front

indicators.note: in front places the distance pieces ahead of the king in the answer

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for foot, a short distance
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: Chasing a monarch who is just ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in front' puts A FT before ER: ER is usually the Queen, but here stands for Edwardus Rex, a King Edward's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: To be after someone is to chase them.

clue.text: West Indian having a place in the order?

definitions.text: having a place in the order?

explanation.surface: A Caribbean islander who belongs to some ordered ranking.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Dominica is a West Indian; a friar of the order of St Dominic also bears the name.

clue.text: For example, dip one in the front of fountain

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the middle of the letters that follow

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dip at the front of a fountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dip' is slang for a pickpocket, not a swim; 'in' places I inside THE plus F.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickpocket is one kind of robber who steals.

clue.text: Animal featured in pop song

explanation.surface: A creature that appears in a hit single.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'pop song' is the nursery rhyme 'Pop Goes the Weasel', not a chart hit.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small carnivorous mammal, and the creature named in the rhyme 'Pop Goes the Weasel'.

clue.text: Churchman endlessly cut biographical verse.

indicators.note: without its end, meaning the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cleric is a churchman
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: A clergyman trims an endless poem about someone's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' takes the final C off CLERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerihew is a comic four-line poem about a famous person, invented by E. C. Bentley.
